jobs.title: Product Manager
jobs.description:
Sprinto is an Autonomous Trust Platform that centralizes trust requirements across security frameworks, vendors, and customers.

Sprinto autonomously executes tasks needed to maintain trust across compliance, audits, risk management, vendor risk, privacy, and AI governance, enabling organizations to maintain a strong, reliable trust posture without draining operational bandwidth and resources on repetitive tasks.

Backed by top-tier investors such as Accel, Elevation, and Blume Ventures, we've raised $31.8M in funding to fuel our mission. Trusted by over 4,000 organizations across 75 countries, Sprinto helps organizations stay audit-ready, manage real-time risks, and scale fearlessly. With 300+ native integrations and AI-driven automation, Sprinto supports 200+ global security standards natively, including SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR, HIPAA, PCI-DSS, and more. Sprinto's extensible architecture enables organizations to build and support an infinite number of custom integrations and frameworks.

Founded in 2020 by second-time founders Girish Redekar and Raghuveer Kancherla, Sprinto powers compliance for organizations like Whatfix, Encora, Anaconda, Whatnot, Ultrahuman, WeWork, Everstage, AI Foundation, HackerRank, and many more.

Life as a Sprinter
responsibilities: Nobody succeeds at Sprinto by staying in their lane.

We are organized around problems, not job titles. Sprinters take ownership beyond their role, solve hard problems, and care deeply about the impact they create. If something can be improved, fixed, or built, we don't wait for permission; we step in.

Being remote means we rely less on proximity and more on trust. We write things down, communicate openly, and move quickly because great teams aren't built by sitting together, they're built by pulling in the same direction.
We believe progress beats perfection, feedback is a gift, and doing the right thing matters, even when nobody is watching.
And while we move with urgency, we never move alone.
Where you'll leave your mark?

Own Sprinto's AI browser extensions and AI features end to end — one of several streams within our AI pod, alongside accuracy baselining and automations — as its business owner, not just its product manager.
Define the problem statement from first principles — figure out what's worth building, why, and for whom, before a line of code is written.
Build the product and take it to first customers — work hands-on with an initial set of customers, one on one, to get it to a successful POC stage.
Drive distribution and adoption — partner with CX, Sales, and Marketing to take what worked in POCs to wider launch and measurable adoption across the customer base.
Own accuracy and quality for AI-driven features — set the bar, know the pitfalls of building on non-deterministic systems, and keep improving output reliability post-launch.
Operate with senior-level autonomy — set direction for this stream, make calls without waiting for a mandate, and be accountable for outcomes, not deliverables.

Job Title: Product Lead Data Management Services

HSBC Data & Analytics Office (DAO) promotes a data-driven culture across HSBC through our strategy of:

Protect: To protect our data we need robust policies for data management and enhanced governance e.g. data that is consumed from a trusted source, meets quality standards, and complies with regulatory obligations.

Connect: Move to a data-led culture through enhanced training including on the job opportunities. Our talent is the glue between protecting our data and unlocking value for our customers.

Unlock. Value is unlocked when we deliver on the opportunities our well-managed data presents e.g. improving customer / colleague experience, increasing revenue, commercialising our data, optimising capital, enhancing risk management or reducing costs.

We are hiring a Product Lead
responsibilities: DMS within Data Management Services (part of Data & Analytics Office)

The Data function owns the bank’s data controls and the ecosystem of tools that allows every business and function to implement and evidence those controls. That ecosystem is being rebuilt: legacy tools are being redesigned, new platforms are being brought in, and the target state is a fully automated, control-by-design data estate, where data quality, lineage, metadata, classification, retention, access and issue management are largely machine-executed rather than manually attested.

We are hiring a Product Lead to own that estate end to end. This is a build-and-scale mandate on a compressed timeline, not a steady-state product management role. The successful candidate will set the product strategy, consolidate a fragmented tooling landscape into a coherent platform, lead the product community, and be personally accountable for landing the target state within an aggressive delivery window.
Governance and Committee Memberships

The jobholder will continually reassess the operational risks associated with the role and inherent in the business, taking account of changing economic or market conditions, legal and regulatory requirements, operating procedures and practices, management restructurings, and the impact of new technology.

The jobholder will also adhere to and be able to demonstrate adherence to internal controls. This will be achieved by adherence to all relevant procedures, keeping appropriate records and, where appropriate, by the timely implementation of internal and external audit points, including issues raised by external regulators.

The jobholder will implement the Group compliance policy by containing compliance risk in liaison with Global Head of Compliance, Global Compliance Officer, Area Compliance Officer or Local Compliance Officer. The term ‘compliance’ embraces all relevant financial services laws, rules and codes with which the business has to comply

Own the DMS product vision and multi-year roadmap to deliver the bank-wide automated data control journey (control-by-design, scalable and measurable). Convert control outcomes into deliverable increments (epics/features) with clear acceptance criteria and benefits tracking (e.g., automation rate, evidence quality, adoption, cycle-time reduction).

Partner with Data Technology and Architecture to define the target state and make explicit buy / build / configure / retire decisions, including legacy rationalisation and decommissioning. Create platform consistency by setting common product standards/patterns across DMS (e.g., workflow, APIs, integration patterns, MI/metrics, auditability) so tools operate as one coherent estate.

Lead and develop the Product Owner community across the DMS portfolio, setting direction, ways of working and a consistent bar for discovery, prioritisation and outcome delivery. Orchestrate delivery through matrix technology teams (without direct line management), aligning priorities, managing dependencies, removing blockers and ensuring shared accountability for outcomes.

Run portfolio-level prioritisation and capacity allocation to ensure engineering effort is focused on the highest-risk/highest-value control outcomes, with realistic sequencing and transparent trade-offs. Establish and operate strong delivery governance to maintain delivery momentum and quality.

Drive adoption and change at scale (training, communications, migrations) ensuring DMS tooling becomes the “path of least resistance” for Data Owners, Data Stewards and control teams. Ensure risk, regulatory and control-by-design compliance: DMS products must meet HSBC standards for security, resilience, data privacy/records management and third-party risk, and provide defensible evidence/MI for Risk, Compliance and Internal Audit.

responsibilities: Marketing
Company Overview:

Abracon is a trusted supplier of leading-edge and innovative electronic components including Frequency Control, Timing, Power, Magnetics, RF and Antenna solutions. Servicing world-class companies across the data communication, transportation, industrial, medical, consumer, aerospace, and defense industries, Abracon accelerates customers’ time-to-market by providing unmatched product solutions, technical expertise, and service excellence.
Position Summary:

We are looking for a motivated, early-career Associate Product Manager to support Abracon's RF & Antennas product line, which includes embedded and external antennas, SAW and LTCC filters, and RF ICs. Reporting to the Senior Product Line Manager, you will handle day-to-day product support for sales, distribution partners, and customers, and contribute to the analysis and launch activities that drive the line's growth — while building the foundation to grow into a Product Line Manager role. This is a hands-on opportunity to learn product management on the connectivity technologies behind IoT, automotive, industrial, and wireless infrastructure designs.
Work Environment:

The successful candidate will be a full-time employee based at Abracon's office in Bangalore, India. A hybrid work-from-home arrangement is available. The role partners closely with the Senior Product Line Manager and headquarters teams in Austin, Texas, and requires regular overlap with U.S. business hours.
Growth Opportunity:
Learn product line management directly from a Senior Product Line Manager, with a clear path toward owning product families and, over time, a product line
Build deep technical expertise in antennas, RF filtering, and wireless connectivity
Support Tier 1 customers and distribution partners worldwide on next-generation wireless designs
Gain cross-functional exposure to sales, engineering, operations, and marketing as part of Abracon's growing Bangalore team
requirements: Bachelor's degree in Electronics & Communication Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field
2–3 years of experience in an engineering, applications, field application, product, or technical sales role, with an electronic component manufacturer or distributor
Working knowledge of RF fundamentals, including impedance matching, S-parameters, and antenna parameters (gain, efficiency, VSWR); hands-on experience with a vector network analyzer is a plus
Familiarity with wireless standards (e.g., Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, cellular/LTE/5G, GNSS, UWB) is a plus
Strong interest in product management and a basic understanding of the product lifecycle
Solid analytical skills with proficiency in Excel, PowerPoint and AI tools.
Clear written and verbal communication skills in English, with the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders
Highly organized and responsive, with the ability to manage multiple requests in a fast-paced environment and work effectively with global teams across time zones

Come join our team! Excellence through teamwork drives the company culture at Abracon. We provide opportunities and support for your professional growth and empower each other in exercising our individual strengths.

With a broad portfolio of passive and electromechanical timing, synchronization, power, connectivity and RF antenna solutions and more, Abracon helps engineers transform their ideas into products that meet future customer needs. For more information about Abracon, visit www.abracon.com

This individual will act as a senior leader responsible for shaping the overarching strategy, driving execution, and ensuring alignment across multiple high-impact healthcare domains (such as core administrative processing, clinical data exchange, and member-centric platforms). As a Principal, you will not own a single product feature but will be responsible for orchestrating value creation across the broader ecosystem. You will connect the dots between disparate enterprise initiatives, drive cohesive data and platform strategies, and mentor product managers to deliver solutions that meet the strategic goals of enGen and our health plan partners.

Key Takeaway (Ideal Candidate Profile) The ideal candidate is a seasoned product strategist with deep expertise in the US payer/provider landscape. They excel at "connecting the dots" across complex enterprise platforms, driving overarching product vision, and influencing executive stakeholders to prioritize high-value, scalable healthcare solutions.

Key
responsibilities: Enterprise Product Strategy & Vision (40%)

Portfolio-Level Roadmap: Define and champion a unified strategic vision that connects roadmaps across various health-tech domains, ensuring they collectively contribute to enterprise goals like operational efficiency, improved health outcomes, and seamless provider/member experiences.

Strategic Decision-Making: Act as the ultimate decision-maker on value sequencing and prioritization for large, cross-domain initiatives. Make informed, data-driven trade-offs that balance short-term client needs with long-term platform scalability.

Innovation & Market Research: Serve as the organization's thought leader on emerging trends in healthcare technology (including automation, advanced analytics, and interoperability). Champion innovative solutions and build compelling, quantitative business cases for new strategic investments. 2. Cross-Functional Orchestration & Governance (35%)

Ecosystem Collaboration: Act as the primary orchestrator between siloed product pillars, engineering leaders, data architecture teams, and business stakeholders. Identify opportunities for reusable solutions (e.g., shared data connectors, enterprise APIs, common business rules) to eliminate redundancy and accelerate delivery.

Stakeholder Influence: Influence stakeholders at all levels, from health plan executives to engineering leads, without direct authority. Articulate complex technical and healthcare business concepts to build consensus and drive alignment across a matrixed organization.

Compliance & Data Governance: Champion enterprise-wide governance standards for data exchange, security, and ethical automation, ensuring all solutions are compliant with healthcare regulations (HIPAA, CMS mandates) and securely manage PHI/PII. 3. Mentorship & Team Enablement (25%)

Product Leadership Mentorship: Provide direct guidance, coaching, and mentorship to Product Managers, Owners, and Business Analysts. Elevate the team's ability to think strategically, prioritize for value, and execute agile methodologies effectively.

Best Practices Evangelism: Define and institutionalize product management best practices, particularly in the areas of data-driven decision-making, value-based prioritization, and outcome-oriented roadmapping.

Talent Development: Partner with leadership to identify skill gaps and develop talent within the product management organization, fostering a culture of continuous learning and operational excellence.
requirements: Extensive Experience: 12+ years of progressive experience in product management, business consulting, or a related strategic role, with a significant portion dedicated to the US healthcare payer or health-tech space.

Healthcare Domain Expertise: Deep subject matter expertise in broad healthcare domains such as health plan operations, claims processing ecosystems, clinical data integration, or provider network management.

jobs.title: Sr Product Manager - Flights OTA
jobs.description:
Own a Flights problem space end-to-end - not a screen, not a funnel stage. Youll take the traveller journey across shopping, booking, and post-booking and be accountable for how it performs commercially and how it behaves when reality intervenes: fares that move, tickets that fail, schedules that change, and travellers who need to cancel.

The scope deliberately spans surfaces. Metasearch and comparison remain central to how travellers find us, but the interesting problems now sit in the seams - where a supplier switch at booking time creates a support contact three days later, where a baggage allowance we didnt parse at search time becomes a refund dispute, where the fare rule we couldnt read at purchase becomes a $700 agency debit memo six months on.

This is an individual contributor role with real leverage. Youll lead cross-functional squads across Engineering, Design, Data Science, Supply, Commercial, Finance Ops, and Customer Support, and youll be measured on outcomes - conversion, traffic quality, provider performance, cost-to-serve, retention - not on shipping velocity.

What youll actually work on

These are live, funded programmes, not aspirations. The detail will shift the shape wont. Here are some examples of problems you ll need to solve.

Zero Touch - self-service refunds and exchanges. Most of our contact-centre volume is travellers asking whether they can cancel or change, and most of them dont proceed once they see the cost. Youll make that answer instant,
responsibilities: 90% accurate is not a pass. In most products a heuristic thats right nine times out of ten is a win. Here, the 10% is a traveller told their ticket was refundable when it wasnt - so we either break a promise or eat the loss - or a void we shouldnt have processed, which returns as an airline debit six months later with a penalty attached. Youll have to reason about failure cost per decision, not aggregate accuracy.
The truth is spread across systems that dont agree. There is no single row you can trust. Much of this work is deciding what the source of truth is before you can automate anything on top of it.

Money moves before the answer is known. Funds have often already gone to the supplier by the time we decide what the traveller is owed. Product decisions here land directly on finance reconciliation, and youll need to design with that in mind rather than hand it over.

Complexity were choosing to keep. Continuous reprice optimization is a significant profit stream. We are not turning it off to make servicing simpler. Youll be automating on top of a system that deliberately mutates bookings after sale.
Some rules only exist in someones head. A real part of this role is operational design: turning tacit knowledge held by a handful of people into something a system - or an AI agent - can act on.

Strategy and vision. Define and evolve the strategy for your Flights problem space, aligned to marketplace growth and commercial objectives. Identify where we can be structurally more competitive, and translate that into measurable outcomes.

Roadmap and delivery. Own the roadmap and its sequencing, prioritising on customer value, business impact, technical feasibility, and dependency risk. Lead initiatives through discovery, validation, delivery, experimentation, launch, and optimisation. Balance near-term commercial wins against foundational platform investment - and be able to defend the trade-off.

Experience quality. Champion a fast, intuitive, and above all truthful experience at every stage. Optimise relevance, price presentation, filtering, comparison, provider selection, fulfilment, and self-service. Validate with research, experimentation, and behavioural data.

Data and performance. Partner with Data Science and Analytics on funnel health. Define and track KPIs across acquisition, engagement, conversion, retention, traffic quality, provider performance, cost-to-serve, and marketplace efficiency.

Cross-functional leadership. Work across Engineering, Design, Supply, Commercial, Marketing, Revenue Management, Finance Ops, and Customer Support. Communicate priorities, decisions, and trade-offs clearly. Build alignment without direct authority.

Market intelligence. Track airline distribution shifts, NDC adoption, competitor moves, and emerging technology - particularly AI applied to fare interpretation and servicing - and turn that into initiatives.

Risk and operational excellence. Surface delivery, technical, commercial, and regulatory risk early. Improve experimentation frameworks and development process. Keep decisions consistent with platform stability and long-term maintainability.

5+ years in Product Management, with direct ownership of customer-facing digital products.
Meaningful experience as a PM in a Flights OTA - a business that sells and services flight tickets. Metasearch, aggregation, comparison, or affiliate-only experience does not substitute for this.

Depth across more than one flights problem space. For example shopping and booking booking and post-booking supply and shopping. We want someone who has seen how decisions in one stage surface as cost or breakage in another.

What You Will Do
responsibilities: Technical Portfolio Strategy and Optimization: Evaluate the existing networking, converter, and console server portfolio to drive SKU rationalization, BOM optimization, and margin improvement. Identify which products to consolidate or sunset and which high-margin lines to scale.

OEM/ODM Vendor Architecture and Management: Act as the primary technical interface with our global manufacturing partners. Influence their roadmaps, negotiate technical SLAs, and drive root-cause analysis and supplier quality corrections for field failures.

Rigorous Product Engineering and QA Leadership: Own the firmware and hardware validation gate. Design and execute New Product Introduction testing, regulatory compliance verification, and automated test frameworks.

Level 3 Escalation Authority: Serve as the final technical escalation point for complex field failures. Perform hands-on debugging in the lab, translate field data into engineering requirements, and enforce corrective actions with vendors.

Engineering Impact of Compliance and Certification: Partner with the Compliance Manager, who tracks market mandates and certification requirements. You translate those mandates into hardware and firmware requirements, evaluating vendor BOMs and architectures so that component or firmware changes do not silently invalidate FIPS, TAA, UL, NERC CIP, and other relevant standards.

Lifecycle and Knowledge Execution: Manage the product lifecycle from NPI through End-of-Life. Build the technical documentation, training material, troubleshooting guides, firmware test checklists, and compatibility matrices that empower support, Product Ops, and adjacent product managers.
Cross-Portfolio Technical Collaboration: Act as the networking subject matter expert for the broader product organization, supporting Sales and Product Marketing with technical content.
Core Technical Expertise

Layer 2 and Layer 3 Networking Standards: VLANs (802.1Q), Spanning Tree Protocols (STP/RSTP/MSTP), link aggregation (LACP), QoS/CoS prioritization, IP routing (Static, OSPF), IGMP snooping, and security mechanisms like 802.1X and ACLs.

Media Conversion and Physical Layer Mechanics: Optical and copper interfaces (SFP/SFP+, RJ-45, single-mode vs. multi-mode fiber, wavelength specifications), Power over Ethernet standards, and rate-matching mechanics.
PoE System Engineering: PSE/PD classification and power budget validation across 802.3af, 802.3at, intelligent detection and backward-compatibility behavior, and downstream device power profiling.

Harsh-Environment and Industrial Specifications: Industrial hardening, wide operating temperatures, high EMC/EMI immunity, redundant power inputs, ring redundancy protocols, and DIN-rail or panel-mount deployment.

DESCRIPTION

The Outbound and Flow team within Amazon Fulfillment Technologies (AFT) is looking for an experienced Product Manager (Technical) to own the vision and strategy for Routing and Mansort products, based out of Bangalore. Our team provides the products and services responsible for outbound fulfillment — ingesting shipments from upstream systems (SCOT) and processing them through picking, packing, and shipping. Our vision is to improve customer experience — Delivery Estimate Accuracy (DEA), Speed, Quality, and Cost — while improving associate safety and simplifying our operations. We do so by building products that are highly reliable, resilient, self-healing, scalable, extensible, and designed from the start with a focus on the safety and accessibility of our workforce.

As a Product Manager (Technical) — L6 for Routing and Mansort, you will define, execute, and deliver a product roadmap that optimizes how units and packages are routed through the fulfillment center and how manual sortation (Mansort) operations are streamlined for throughput, quality, and cost. You will strongly influence the strategy and vision for the group, and develop and maintain product roadmaps and features grounded in team strategy. This role is inherently cross-functional — you will work closely with engineering, science, operations, and business teams across geographies to launch features and build the tools and mechanisms that scale Routing and Mansort worldwide.

responsibilities: Define product vision, strategy, and roadmap priorities by working backward from customer needs, conducting research, analyzing usage data and market trends, and translating insights into clear problem statements and requirements.

responsibilities: As an Associate Product Manager on the VMDR team, you'll help define how security and IT teams discover, assess, prioritize and remediate vulnerabilities across on-prem, cloud, container and remote assets. Success is measured in real risk reduction (TruRisk), not raw finding counts.

This role is for early-career problem-solvers with hands-on vulnerability management experience who want to grow into a full product manager. You'll own well-scoped features end to end and learn alongside senior PMs, engineering and Threat Research.
1. Product definition and roadmap

Own and evolve well-scoped features in core VMDR modules such as Asset Discovery & Inventory, Vulnerability Detection (Cloud Agent, network scanners, passive sensors), TruRisk Prioritization (QDS, threat intel, CISA KEV, EPSS), Dashboards & Reporting, and Remediation (Patch Management, TruRisk Eliminate).
Collaborate with engineering to define product requirements and specifications: PRDs, user stories, prioritization logic, workflows, wireframe annotations and acceptance criteria.
Assist in developing the product roadmap and feature prioritization using frameworks such as RICE or MoSCoW, balancing customer asks, competitive gaps and engineering effort.
Groom the backlog in Jira, prioritize with engineering, QA and UX, and track delivery against quarterly release plans.
2. Vulnerability assessment and threat analysis
Perform hands-on vulnerability assessments: run authenticated and agent-based scans, review detections, investigate false positives/negatives and validate detection coverage.

Conduct threat analysis on high-impact CVEs and zero-days (exploit availability, ransomware and malware association, CISA KEV listing, EPSS trend) with Threat Research, and turn findings into detection and prioritization requirements.
Translate concepts such as CVSS vs. EPSS vs. QDS, asset criticality, toxic combinations, SLA breaches and MTTR into product features with measurable risk reduction.
Test and validate features before release: scans, detections, QQL queries, dashboards, reports and APIs.
preferred: Must-have qualifications
Experience
25 years in product management, product analyst, technical program, solutions/sales engineering, or security engineering/analyst roles.
At least 1 year working directly on vulnerability management, security operations, or a cybersecurity product (SaaS preferred).
Domain knowledge (must be able to explain in an interview)
Vulnerability management lifecycle: asset discovery and inventory scanning (authenticated vs unauthenticated, agent vs network) prioritization remediation/patching verification and reporting.
CVE, CWE, NVD, CVSS scoring, EPSS, CISA KEV, and the difference between severity and risk.
Patch management, configuration management and asset management basics across Windows, Linux and cloud workloads.

QAD is a leading provider of ERP solutions purpose-built for manufacturing industries — automotive, life sciences, food & beverage, high tech, and industrial. Serving thousands of global manufacturers, QAD's Adaptive Manufacturing Cloud helps companies operate with greater precision, agility, and intelligence.

Enterprise software is entering a third era. The first gave manufacturers a System of Record — ERP that answered 'what do we have and what did we commit to?' The second gave them Data Infrastructure — the ability to move, analyse, and query that data at scale. The third era is domain-specific intelligence: AI agents that can act autonomously on manufacturing data, but only if that data has been given the context, relationships, and governed rules that allow an agent to reason correctly.

ERA — QAD's Enterprise Resource Allocation platform — is the domain intelligence layer that sits between any ERP and any AI agent. It encodes what manufacturing data means, governs what agents are permitted to do, and makes every autonomous decision traceable and accountable.

Senior Product Manager, Search, Indexing and Query

Couchbase | Product Organisation | Bangalore, India | Reports to VP of AI Product Management
responsibilities: Couchbase is building the operational data platform for AI. Search, indexing and query are the core of it — how data is found, filtered, ranked and returned is what determines whether an application, or an agent, can actually use the data underneath. We are hiring a Senior Product Manager to own that surface area across Capella and Couchbase Enterprise: the SQL++ query experience, secondary indexing, full-text search, and vector and hybrid search.

This is a hands-on individual contributor role for someone who wants to do the work at the Senior level — write the PRFAQ, sit with the customer, push the tradeoff, ship the capability, and own the outcome after launch. Reporting to the VP of AI Product Management, you will partner closely with the query, indexing and search engineering teams, with sales and GTM, and with the broader AI organization.
You do not need to have shipped a query engine or a search product before. We are hiring for the underlying capability, not the resume line — see “Who This Role Is Open To” below.
What You Will Own

Search, indexing and query as a product surface: End-to-end ownership of how customers express and satisfy a query on Couchbase — SQL++ query, global secondary indexes, full-text search, and vector and hybrid search. The roadmap in your area, the PRFAQs and PRDs, the launch, the adoption, and the iteration after launch.

Retrieval for AI applications: Make Couchbase the retrieval layer that RAG applications and agents actually use — hybrid search relevance, metadata filtering, recall and freshness, and cost per query. Work with the wider AI portfolio so retrieval composes with the rest of the platform rather than sitting beside it.

Developer experience for query and indexing: How a developer writes a query, gets an index recommendation, debugs a slow plan, and understands what a query costs. Reduce the number of things a developer has to know before their first query is fast.

Performance, cost and benchmark credibility: Own the performance story for your area. Reproducible benchmarks the field can stand behind, a defensible cost and TCO narrative against MongoDB, Elastic, Postgres and pgvector, and dedicated vector stores, and a clear point of view on where Couchbase wins and where it does not.

Working backwards from the customer: Start with the customer and work backwards. Write the PRFAQ before any code is written. Validate with real, named enterprise customers. Make clear tradeoff calls about what to build and what to defer based on what the enterprise ICP universally needs — not features chasing competitors or one-off requests outside the ICP.

Engineering partnership: Work shoulder-to-shoulder with the query, indexing and search engineering teams. Earn their trust by being technically credible, decisive on scope, and clear on the why. Own the PRD as a living document, not a one-time artifact. Hold the bar on quality, scope, and timing through to launch.

Customer and design partner engagement: Run design partner programs for the capabilities you own. Bring real customer voice into roadmap decisions and back to the broader team. Help build a pipeline of named reference customers willing to talk publicly about what they have shipped.

Cross-portfolio collaboration: Coordinate across Core Database, Capella, Analytics, Mobile and Edge, and the AI Specialist team so the capabilities you own compose cleanly with the rest of the platform. Bring a build-vs-partner point of view to your area.
requirements: Seven or more years in product management, with at least three on a technical platform — database, data infrastructure, search, analytics, developer tools, cloud infrastructure, or AI infrastructure.

Systems depth. You can reason about latency, throughput, recall, index structures, query plans, memory and storage tradeoffs, and cost per operation. Given a benchmark or a slow query, you know what to ask next.

Customer obsession and working-backwards rigor: You start with the customer and work backwards. You write PRFAQs before code. You can tell which feature requests reflect universal ICP needs and which are noise, and you make the call clearly.
Engineering credibility: Engineers want to work with you. You hold your own on architecture, are decisive on scope, and own the why behind every tradeoff.
Cross-functional trust: Sales trusts your roadmap. GTM trusts your enablement. Marketing trusts your narrative. You build durable working relationships outside your own team.
AI-driven PM practice: You already use AI in your own PM work — research, PRFAQ drafting, customer synthesis, competitive analysis — and you can point to concrete examples.

QAD is a leading provider of ERP solutions purpose-built for manufacturing industries — automotive, life sciences, food & beverage, high tech, and industrial. Serving thousands of global manufacturers, QAD's Adaptive Manufacturing Cloud helps companies operate with greater precision, agility, and intelligence.

QAD's AI Platform is the domain intelligence layer that sits between the ERP and autonomous AI agents. It encodes what manufacturing data means, governs what agents are permitted to do, and makes every autonomous decision traceable and accountable — transforming QAD from a system of record into a system of action.

Job Description

This role owns the full product lifecycle for QAD's Copilot, Search, and Conversational Analytics capabilities — from architecture through to market launch. You will define what gets built, why it matters to manufacturing users, and how it reaches them: shaping the product vision, driving engineering delivery, and partnering with GTM to ensure adoption.

The intelligence that powers these surfaces — how queries are understood, how manufacturing context is assembled, how data is retrieved, and how responses are generated — is where QAD's AI moat is built. You will need to engage deeply with these layers, not as an engineer but as the product owner who defines the contracts, quality standards, and sequencing decisions that determine whether they work in production at enterprise scale.

You will report
responsibilities: Copilot & Conversational Analytics
Own the product definition for QAD's Copilot: how queries are understood, context assembled, data retrieved, and responses generated — specifying the contracts that engineering builds against

Define the grounding contract: the rules that ensure every Copilot response cites governed manufacturing data, not hallucinated inference — including confidence signalling and graceful fallback behaviour
Drive the conversational analytics strategy: how natural language queries translate into analytical results across manufacturing data domains without exposing SQL or BI complexity to the user
Specify the disambiguation model: how the Copilot handles ambiguous queries, missing context, and conflicting data signals in real manufacturing workflows
Search
Own the product definition for QAD's semantic search layer: indexing strategy, query understanding, entity recognition, ranking, and result structure across manufacturing data domains

Define the search intent taxonomy — operational (find order, trace shipment), analytical (show trends, compare periods), and diagnostic (why is this delayed, what caused this variance) — and specify result formats by intent type
Drive the federated search architecture: how results from ERP operational data, analytical stores, and the knowledge graph are ranked and merged into a coherent, useful response
Discovery, Delivery & GTM
Maintain a structured customer discovery programme — extracting real manufacturing query patterns and translating findings into specific product and architecture implications
Own the product backlog: writing stories to Staff Engineer level of specificity — API contracts, state machines, data flows, edge cases — that engineering can build without verbal clarification
requirements: Product Experience
7–12 years in product management, with significant time owning AI-powered, search, or analytics products in enterprise B2B environments — from definition through production launch
Proven track record owning the full product lifecycle: customer discovery, specification, engineering delivery, and GTM — not just one slice
Experience working in matrixed organisations — driving outcomes across Platform, Engineering, Architecture, and GTM without direct authority
Evidence of structured discovery practice applied to a technical product surface — ability to extract product implications from user research, not just UX insights
Core Technical Depth — Required
These are the primary technical domains this role owns. Strong command is expected from day one.
Semantic search architecture: indexing strategy, query understanding, entity recognition, ranking models, and relevance evaluation at enterprise scale
Conversational AI product design: how natural language queries are translated into structured analytical results across complex, domain-specific data without exposing backend complexity to users

LLM-integrated product specification: grounding strategies, hallucination mitigation, response quality gates, and context window management — sufficient to define product contracts engineering builds against

Data platform fluency: OLAP vs operational DB reads, federated search across heterogeneous stores, and how data freshness constraints affect product quality — sufficient to hold authoritative conversations with data engineers
SQL and data modelling: sufficient to validate query plans, understand schema implications, and reason through retrieval architecture trade-offs

QuickBooks is Intuit's flagship accounting software, powering millions of small and mid-sized businesses globally. The Mid-Market team is driving a critical transformation: migrating customers from Desktop to cloud-native platforms.

Today, migration from desktop to cloud is high-friction and high-touch. It slows conversion and strains support capacity. Your mission is to change that by building an AI Agent that guides customers through the entire migration journey, from readiness assessment to data migration, configuration, and first productive use.

requirements: Experience: 10+ years in product management with 2+ years shipping AI agent, conversational AI, or intelligent automation products in B2B SaaS or Fintech.

Function Product Leadership, AI Infrastructure (Velocis)

Why this role, why now?

Neysa is building the AI cloud for the era where AI runs in production rather than in pilots. The promise we are claiming to deliver is operational confidence, the ability for an enterprise to run AI predictably, affordably and accountably. Infrastructure choices now decide which AI programmes are viable at all, and for us sovereignty means strategic control rather than a compliance checkbox.

Velocis is how we deliver that, across GPU as a service and our AI platform as a service. We are scaling from strong early proof into a platform that serves sovereign enterprise buyers in India and large offtake capacity globally. This role exists to help set product direction and to make it real.
responsibilities: We are hiring a Senior Director of Product to sit alongside the Chief Product Officer as a balanced strategist and operator, and to co-own the Velocis product ecosystem. You will help shape the two-year product strategy and you will own the roadmap, prioritisation and specification sign-off that turn it into shipped platform. Engineering, infrastructure operations, design and go-to-market are your delivery partners, and product holds the pen on what gets built and in what order.
You will move between whiteboarding high-density cluster architecture with an executive buyer in one hour and running a deep specification review with a product manager in the next. Both are the job.
What you will own?Product strategy and roadmap
Co-own the 12 and 24 month strategy for Velocis across GPU as a service and the AI platform, and hold the roadmap, prioritisation and specification sign-off end to end.
Ship the Velocis AI platform stack and move straight into post-launch feature velocity, reliability, and the Day-0 and Day-1 user journey.
Keep a live read on the global AI infrastructure landscape, across orchestration layers, sovereign cloud, inference economics and power and density, so Velocis holds its edge.
Team and craft
Lead, mentor and hold accountable a team of four or more product managers across the core Velocis modules.
Build a product culture of extreme ownership, technical precision and fast feedback, and raise the hiring bar as the team grows.
Coach high-potential talent and step in where a track needs lift.
Enterprise commercials and offtake
Partner with the CPO and CEO on offtake opportunities from 1,000 to 8,000 GPUs, shaping orchestration specs, tenant isolation and SLA commitments.
requirements: Ten or more years in product management, with four or more leading product teams. Hands-on experience in GPU computing, AI or ML orchestration or HPC is ideal, and strong candidates from adjacent large-scale cloud or general-purpose cloud infrastructure, with the ability to ramp fast, will be considered.
A track record of shipping complex B2B infrastructure products from concept to meaningful revenue scale.

Fluency across GPU infrastructure on NVIDIA and AMD, container and workload orchestration such as Kubernetes, Slurm and Ray, VPC and network topologies, object storage and dedicated inference pipelines.

Working command of multi-tenancy and tenant isolation, observability and cost attribution, sovereign deployment patterns such as air-gapped clusters and customer-managed keys, and inference economics measured as cost per token and P99 latency.
Commercial fluency, so that you connect product decisions to gross margin, resource efficiency and customer return.
How you work?
You zoom out to market positioning and a two-year horizon, and zoom in to specifications, telemetry and the granular detail, without losing either.
You have a default to action and high standards, and you pair them with the judgment to say no and to sequence well.
You are a low-ego and articulate communicator who earns credibility quickly with engineers, enterprise CTOs and executive leadership.
You are comfortable building in a category that is still being created.

Take full ownership of the roadmap and prioritisation across the PM tracks, with clear ownership lines in place.

Wise is building the best way to move and manage money across borders. We need someone to help us move money seamlessly in APAC.

We process hundreds of millions of payments for our customers per year. When Wise started we used banks to power our payments. But as we’ve grown we’ve started connecting directly to national payment schemes such as Australia’s NPP, Singapore’s FAST, Philippines' InstaPay, and Japan’s Zengin.

We’re looking for a Product Manager to lead our efforts in integrating and optimising national payment scheme integrations across the APAC region. responsibilities: Understand customer needs: Build an understanding of how payment schemes impact our customers, and use this understanding to drive product decisions.

Description

What if running an e-commerce business could become dramatically simpler — with AI helping sellers manage orders, inventory, pricing and operations across every channel they sell on?

Amazon Smart Commerce is looking for a Principal Product Manager
responsibilities: Tech to lead SmartHub (including the team of PMs), our multi-channel commerce operations platform. SmartHub brings together orders, inventory, catalog, returns, warehousing and business insights across marketplaces and D2C channels into a single system, helping businesses operate at scale without navigating multiple disconnected tools.

We are now at an exciting inflection point. Advances in generative and agentic AI create an opportunity to fundamentally rethink how sellers operate their businesses — moving from dashboards and workflows that tell sellers what happened, toward intelligent experiences that understand their business, identify what needs attention, recommend actions and increasingly execute work on their behalf.

As the Principal PM for SmartHub, you will define this next chapter. You will own the long-term product vision and roadmap for SmartHub and lead important horizontal capabilities such as pricing that span the broader Smart Commerce portfolio.

Reimagine high-frequency seller workflows such as order processing, inventory management, exception handling, returns and pricing to make operating across multiple sales channels dramatically simpler.

jobs.description:
ABOUT DBMCI ONE

DBMCI One is a learning platform for medical students and doctors, a product of NHPL (Neuroglia Health Private Limited), a subsidiary of M3, Inc., Japan's largest healthcare company, listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

NHPL is also the company behind Marrow, India's largest and most trusted learning platform for NEET PG preparation.

DBMCI One brings together the legacy of Dr. Bhatia's Medical Coaching Institute, trusted by generations of medical aspirants, with the product velocity and data discipline of a modern tech company. We are building the definitive learning platform for India's next generation of doctors: one that adapts to how each aspirant learns, making the journey from preparation to practice measurably better.

The stakes are real. The ambition is bigger.
responsibilities: We are looking for a Product Manager to own the learner growth and engagement charter at DBMCI One. This is not a coordination role. It is a high-ownership position where you define what keeps a medical student coming back every day, what drives them from trial to deep engagement, and what ultimately makes them succeed.

You are joining at an inflection point. The habits and learning outcomes you shape today will determine how thousands of medical students learn, and in turn, how they diagnose, treat, and care for millions of patients tomorrow.
You will work hand-in-hand with Engineering, Design, Content, Data, and Marketing to ship a product that moves real numbers and real lives.
AI is not a tool you will be asked to explore here. It is the default. You are expected to prototype, automate, and iterate using AI natively from day one.
WHAT YOU'LL OWN
Own the full growth loop: Activation Engagement Habit Formation Retention for DBMCI One learners across platforms.
Define and drive the product roadmap for learner-facing features, from discovery through experimentation, launch, and post-launch iteration.
Use AI-assisted prototyping and vibe-coding tools to independently build and test product ideas, reducing dependence on full engineering cycles for early validation.
Design and run GTM experiments: scope the hypothesis, build a lean version, get it in front of real users, gather feedback, and iterate fast before committing to a full build.
Design and run A/B experiments at pace. Test hypotheses, kill what does not work, and double down on what does.
Conduct structured user research: interviews, session analysis, and cohort studies to uncover the real reasons learners drop off or stay hooked.
Identify leading indicators of learner success and build features that move them, not vanity metrics.
requirements: 2 to 4 years of Product Management experience at a tech-first company. Consumer internet, EdTech, or mobile-first products are strongly preferred.
Strong product thinking grounded in user behaviour. You can articulate the "why behind the why" for any user action or drop-off.
Hands-on data fluency: SQL, funnel analysis, cohort analysis, and A/B experiment design. You live in data, not just talk about it.

AI fluency is non-negotiable. Proficient with AI-assisted prototyping and vibe-coding tools (Cursor, Bolt, Lovable, Replit, or similar). Practical experience with agentic AI workflows, automation, and prompt engineering applied to product work.
Technical fluency: You can hold a system design conversation with Engineering, understand API dependencies, and make informed build-vs-scope decisions.
Proven ability to run end-to-end GTM experiments: scope, build, launch, gather user feedback, and iterate with speed and structure.
First-principles thinker. You do not copy-paste frameworks; you reason from the user and the context up.
High ownership, low excuses. You move fast, learn faster, and take full responsibility for what ships and what it achieves.
Clear, structured communicator. You can align a cross-functional team with a well-framed problem statement and a sharp point of view.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager
jobs.description:
Overview

The Windows + Devices Fundamentals team builds and operates data platforms and backend services that help teams improve Windows performance, power efficiency, and reliability. We connect signals from labs and the installed base to trustworthy metrics, actionable diagnostics, and measurable improvements in responsiveness, battery life, memory efficiency, and device health.

We are looking for a Senior Product Manager to own a data and services product area that turns these signals into effective engineering workflows. You will define product and measurement strategy, set priorities across related capabilities, and partner with engineering and data science from customer discovery through delivery and adoption. This is a hands-on technical PM role: you should be comfortable querying data, reasoning about service behavior, and connecting platform investments to better customer experiences.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
responsibilities: Product direction: Own the strategy and roadmap for a data and services product area. Understand engineering teams' needs and prioritize reusable capabilities that address common problems, rather than one-off reports.

Data products: Define requirements across telemetry ingestion, transformation, orchestration, storage, and APIs. Partner on schema evolution, data quality, freshness, privacy, and access control so downstream consumers can trust and use the data.

Measurement and analysis: Establish metric definitions, baselines, and cohorts across devices, silicon, and customer segments. Use SQL/KQL and statistical reasoning to investigate metric movements, distinguish regressions from measurement changes, and guide investments.

Service fundamentals: Partner with engineering on service-level objectives, observability, scale, latency, availability, and cost. Define safe-release criteria and balance new capabilities with service health, security, compliance, and learning from live-site incidents.

Windows outcomes: Help define measurable targets and regression guardrails for responsiveness, battery life, memory efficiency, and reliability. Connect insights to prioritized engineering action and track whether changes improve customer scenarios.

Cross-team delivery: Align engineering, data science, security, and partner PM teams on scope, dependencies, and tradeoffs. Drive delivery across related feature areas, resolve ambiguity, and raise risks early.

Automation and adoption: Prioritize self-service diagnostics, alerting, and validated AI-assisted analysis that help teams detect issues earlier and reduce manual investigation. Measure adoption, diagnostic effectiveness, time saved, and impact on Windows fundamentals.
Technical leadership: Communicate complex findings and tradeoffs clearly. Strengthen product thinking through knowledge sharing, mentorship, and inclusive collaboration.

jobs.description:

Refold AI is the AI integration platform built for agents, made for modern SaaS companies that need to ship enterprise integrations at scale. We're reimagining integrations with AI agents that work like business consultants and integration engineers, building them 10x faster, in hours instead of days. You win the enterprise deals that hinge on them, onboard faster, and scale without an army of consultants.

We've grown rapidly, reaching seven-figure ARR and 30+ paying customers, powering the product and professional services teams at modern SaaS companies, from Incorta, Kantata, and Coupa to Highradius, Naehas, and OvationCXM.

responsibilities: Where does automation earn trust, and where does a human still need to stay in the loop?

You will draw that line repeatedly, and the answer will keep changing. How do you price outcomes instead of usage, in an industry that has only ever paid for hours? You will own that question commercially and build the model around it. What does it mean for a platform to get smarter across customers without leaking what any one customer knows?
You will define what learning looks like at the system level.
How do ISV developers think about reliability when their customers depend on
integrations running without anyone watching? You will own that experience end to end.
When something breaks in production for an enterprise customer, who gets told, what do they see, and what can they do about it? You will design that judgment layer.
requirements: You have shipped something on your own. A side project, a tool, anything you took from zero to working. We are building systems with real complexity. We need someone who has felt the difference between a decision made in a doc and a decision made in code.

You think in constraints. When you look at a feature request, the first question is what breaks if we build this, not what we could do with it. Edge cases are not polish. They are often the product.
You write, not deck. Specs, trade-off docs, design decisions. If you cannot write a crisp two-page spec, the feature is not ready to build.
You push back. If the scoping is underspecified, say so. If the deadline is not realistic, say so. Disagree clearly and commit once a decision is made

At least 2 of those years on a platform, infrastructure, or developer tool.

Track record of shipping things that were actually hard, not feature additions on a stable roadmap

Join Amazon Pharmacy's Supply Chain team and shape the systems that determine how medications reach patients. You will define product strategy and drive performance for the buying and inventory planning systems at the core of the pharmacy supply chain: procurement systems that decide what to buy and when under expiry and regulatory constraints, inventory planning that sets optimal stock levels across the network, and placement algorithms that position inventory across fulfillment centers. These systems are informed by demand forecasts that predict prescription volume, but your focus is turning that signal into smart purchasing and inventory decisions.

Pharmacy supply chains are unlike retail: demand is primarily driven by prescriptions (not browsing), products expire, controlled substances require compliance layers, and regulations vary by state. Every buying and inventory decision you define and measure operates under these constraints.

We are looking for a dynamic, analytically rigorous Senior Product Manager

DESCRIPTION

Join Amazon Pharmacy's Fulfillment Product team and shape the systems that determine how medications are dispensed, verified, and shipped to patients. You will execute the product roadmap to drive performance for the 1P Warehouse Management System (WMS) — the unified platform being built on AFT (Amazon Fulfillment Technologies) primitives to orchestrate pharmacy fulfillment within the four walls.

Pharmacy fulfillment is unlike retail: workflows span controlled substance compliance (DEA chain-of-custody), cold chain handling, pharmacist verification gates, and dynamic re-routing for problem states — all under HIPAA constraints. Every system you define and measure operates within these regulatory and operational realities, across small-format sites, regional fulfillment centers, and kiosks.

jobs.title: Principal Product Manager
responsibilities: Agentic Investigation & Reliability Experiences
Sumo Logic is hiring a Principal Product Manager to lead how engineers and operators investigate incidents, understand reliability risk, and act on their operational and security telemetry.

The observability category was built around collecting telemetry and giving people tools to navigate it: dashboards, queries, monitors, traces, and alerts. Customer expectations are now shifting. Teams don't just want more dashboards; they want help getting from a signal to a resolution, understanding what's broken, why, what's impacted, and what to do next. As AI agents move into production operations, this role owns how Sumo Logic brings intelligent, agent-assisted investigation and reliability workflows to customers, grounded in evidence, context, and enterprise governance.

This is a senior, high-ownership role. It requires genuine observability domain background. You should have lived in this space and understand how monitoring, troubleshooting, and reliability actually work, combined with the ambition to define a new category of experience on top of it.
What You Will Own
The current data experiences.

Log Search, Live Tail, query and query optimization, Metrics Search, Tracing, Dashboards, and the data-experience UI. This is a live, revenue-generating product with real customers, and keeping it strong is part of the job. You own its health, roadmap, and competitiveness today while steering it toward an AI-native future, focusing new investment where it strengthens investigation, speed, and value for both new and power users.
The reliability and alerting surface.

Monitors, Alerts, SLOs, Scheduled Searches, and the reliability workflows around them. You will own alerting accuracy, noise reduction, and operational health signals both as capabilities customers depend on today and as the foundation for more automated, agent-assisted detection and investigation.
The agentic investigation experience.

You will define how a user moves from a search, a monitor, a dashboard, or an alert to likely cause faster, with supporting evidence. This means productizing investigation workflows that reason across logs, metrics, traces, monitors, dashboards, and related context, and evolving them from reactive troubleshooting toward more proactive detection over time.
What You Will Be Doing
requirements: 8+ years of product management experience with real observability or monitoring domain background. You have owned products in observability, monitoring, incident response, APM, or a closely adjacent operational-telemetry space. This is a hard requirement.

Deep, first-hand understanding of the observability surface area including logs, metrics, traces, dashboards, monitors, alerts, and SLOs, and of how engineers and operators actually investigate incidents and decide what to trust.
Proven ability to run a live, at-scale product, owning the roadmap, health, and competitiveness of shipping surfaces while driving a larger transformation.
A track record of owning broad, technically deep surfaces and setting direction that other teams build on.
Familiarity with how AI and agents are changing data interaction, including natural-language investigation, tools, guardrails, and human-in-the-loop action, or the ability to ramp quickly.

Strong technical instincts around query engines, time-series and trace data, and alerting systems, plus the judgment to know where an AI-assisted experience should replace a manual flow and where depth must stay.
Strong analytical skills and comfort using telemetry, dashboards, SQL, and usage data to understand adoption, friction, reliability, and cost.
Excellent communication across technical and business audiences, and the ability to write clear proposals, decision docs, PRDs, and acceptance criteria.
High ownership and drive to make progress across a large, ambiguous, fast-moving surface.
Must-Have Qualities
Runs today, builds tomorrow.
Keeps a live product healthy and competitive while reinventing it, and knows what to sustain and what to rebuild.

jobs.title: Product Manager
responsibilities: Hevo
The Hard Thing About Data

Most companies that claim to have a "data platform" have a dashboard with some charts and a dream. Hevo has something different. Something that took eight years to build and can't be bought. Over 2,000 companies send us their most sensitive data every single day. 100 billion events a month. Raw. Unfiltered. Before transformation, before aggregation, at the exact moment truth is created. That's not a product feature. That's trust, earned one customer at a time, over eight years, by not screwing up.

That position is now the foundation for something much bigger. We're building an Intelligence Layer on top of it, a system that reads across every data source a company runs, connects the signals that matter, and tells people what to do before they have to go looking for answers. We call it the Context Graph. It's real enough to show results. Early enough that the person who joins now defines what it becomes.
This is the moment. Not the moment after it's obvious. Now.
What You're Walking Into

You'll own a product pod. SaaS integrations, database connectors, or the Intelligence Layer, depending on where the biggest need is when you join. You own the backlog. More importantly, you own the why behind everything that gets built. You report directly to the CEO. In the first 3-6 months, your job is to make the foundation bulletproof, find the gaps in the platform, close them, and make the product sharper than it's ever been. After that, you move into the Intelligence Layer and help define what Hevo becomes in its next chapter.
What This Job Actually Is

Let's be honest about what great PMs do, and what mediocre ones do instead. Mediocre PMs write specs and hand them off. They synthesize feedback from CSMs and call it customer insight. They sit in architecture meetings and nod. They measure their own output in documents shipped, not outcomes delivered. That's not this job. This job is three things, done well, simultneously.

First: technical ownership. You will be in the room when architecture decisions get made. Not watching. Contributing. Pushing back. Asking the questions that change the direction of the decision. You need to understand how data pipelines work at a systems level, CDC, connectors, streaming, schema management, failure modes. If you can't hold your own in that room, engineering will stop inviting you to it. And they'll be right to.

Second: direct customer engagement. You talk to customers yourself. No intermediary. No secondhand summary. You hear the problem in the customer's own words, you sit with the complexity of it, and you own the translation into product decisions. If you're relying on a CSM to tell you what customers need, you will always be one step behind.

Third: making complexity simple. Hevo's product is deeply technical. The people who sell it and support it are not always. A big part of your job is taking complex system behavior and making it crisp and understandable, for Support, for CS, for Solutions Engineering, so they can represent the product confidently to customers. If internal teams are confused, customers will be too.

Job Description Summary

Drives product strategy and roadmap for solutions within the Primavera CoE portfolio, partnering with business stakeholders to maximize business value and reuse across GE Vernova. Leads globally distributed technical teams to execute multiple interdependent projects and meet On Time Delivery (OTD) targets. Partners with development leadership and cross-functional teams to translate ambiguous business needs into actionable work and resolve execution roadblocks. Influences program direction and investment priorities, providing technical leadership and mentorship to Technical Product Managers across the organization

Job Description

The Sr Staff Technical Product Manager
responsibilities: DT (Digital Technology) fosters a strong and effective partnership with various functions, including project management, contract management, logistics, finance, sourcing, and more, focusing on Project Execution within Gas Power HDGT and across GE Vernova. This role involves providing the necessary processes, tools, and applications to execute projects and achieve business goals. The role includes driving and implementing business specific or global solutions that utilize other Primavera CoE solutions.

As a member of the Primavera CoE, you will be tasked with defining and executing strategic roadmaps, focusing on initiatives that support business objectives and meet On Time Delivery (OTD) targets. By leveraging key technologies, processes, and domain expertise, you will drive execution across multiple interdependent projects within a program. You will manage interfaces across applications that support and drive cross-functional and cross-system initiatives around Oracle Primavera P6, Pulse (homegrown platform), UDC (Unified Data Center - homegrown platform), Time Control, Safran and Oracle Primavera Unifier.

You will lead globally distributed vendor teams, ensuring they meet Safety Quality Delivery Cost (SQDC) targets and requirements. You will provide tactical direction, balancing the development of new capabilities, driving reuse, maintenance activities, issue resolution, technical debt, vulnerability management, and addressing the latest business priorities to enhance the team's quality, efficiency, and effectiveness.

This role is crucial in ensuring consistency in platforms, tools, software architecture, and data integration strategy within your domains and across the GE Vernova application landscape. Additionally, you will define standard work within your domain of responsibility and establish lean execution standards and processes for project teams. You will also drive utilization of AI tools such as Claude Code across the team as part of these activities.

Act as the owner of platforms (multiple instances), applications and the satellite tools, within the CoE portfolio
Drive the program in accordance with Application Ownership standard work processes.
Partner with business stakeholders to define platform strategy, drive adoption, and maintain a product roadmap aligned with business value.
Identify and drive implementation of cross-business solutions that deliver greater business value and increase reuse opportunities.
Own and manage the backlog, continuously prioritizing based on validated customer problems, business needs, and strategic objectives to ensure PI and sprint readiness.
Own the short-term roadmap for MVPs and quarterly releases.
Translate unstructured or ambiguous work requests into actionable user stories and work units.

jobs.description:
Bluecore is a marketing technology company that’s reimagining how the world’s fastest-growing retail brands transform casual shoppers into lifetime customers. Through our patented retail data model and the recent release of Bluecore Communicate™ and Bluecore Site™, we replace manual processes with an intelligent, AI-driven workflow. We are credited with doubling email revenue, and growing customer retention for more than 400 brands, including Express, Tommy Hilfiger, The North Face, Teleflora, and Bass Pro Shops. We have been recognized as one of the Best Places to Work by Glassdoor and ranked No. 241 on the Inc. 500 List, the most prestigious ranking of the nation’s fastest-growing private companies.

In this role, you will own one of Bluecore’s channels and foster and grow our existing product offering under Bluecore SiteTM. As an enterprise multi-channel personalization platform, Bluecore is an industry leader. You will need to understand how customers drive value from personalization within channels in and out, including general best practices.  This is inherently a cross-functional role -- you will work closely with engineering, design, program management, marketing and sales teams to envision and execute business opportunities.
responsibilities: Articulate the channel strategy and translate this into product requirements and prioritization with our engineers.
Define and prioritize scaling needs as we onboard new customers, grow existing customers, and expand internationally
Manage trade-offs and prioritization between engineering level-of-effort and customer experiences.
Ability to make hypotheses, test with monitoring of data, organize the insights and identify ways to improve efficiency.
requirements: 5+ years as a Product Manager for an enterprise or SaaS software product.
5+ years of experience independently driving and managing complex products within owned marketing channels
Experience coordinating requirements across diverse customer sets.
Customer-centric with a proven track-record of developing and acting on customer insights.
Ability to define opportunities and problems, collect and analyze data, establish facts and make valid conclusions.
Ability to work with cross-functional teams and thrive in a fast-growing, rapidly-changing environment
Experience in MarTech is strongly preferred.
A background in software engineering is a plus.
Knowledge of Agile process and principles

We are proud of the culture of flexibility, inclusivity and trust that we have built around our workforce. We are a remote first organization with the option to potentially work in our New York headquarters on occasion moving forward. We love the opportunity to come together – but employees will always have the option on where they work best.

At Bluecore we believe in encouraging an inclusive environment in which employees feel encouraged to share their unique perspectives, demonstrate their strengths, and act authentically. We know that diverse teams are strong teams, and welcome those from all backgrounds and varying experiences. Bluecore is a proud equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fair hiring practices and to building a welcoming environment for all team members. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, age, familial status or veteran status.

We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodation.
